claim: Hob is released under the MIT license by Frigade.
Hob ships for Mac (Apple Silicon), Windows (x64) and Linux (x86_64).
Hob picks among Gemma 4 sizes by memory and uses gpt-oss 120B on workstations.
quote: Google's Gemma 4 for most computers (E4B Compact on 8 GB Macs, E4B on 16 GB, 26B from 24 GB) and OpenAI's gpt-oss 120B for workstations.

claim: Models run locally via llama.cpp; no telemetry; web access can be turned off.
quote: Chats and files stay on your machine, and there is no telemetry.

claim: Python code runs sandboxed to the chat's folder; changes require approval and can be undone.
quote: Approval confirmations before anything in your folders changes, Undo for every task, and code runs in a sandbox.

claim: Built with Electron and llama.cpp in a separate process.
quote: I build it using Electron bridged with llama.cpp in its own process.

claim: Small models claimed tool results without calling tools or looped; author built guards instead of prompt tweaks.
quote: I spent a fair amount of the work building guards vs tweaking prompts (that didn't really work for small models).

claim: Code guard checks whether files a reply names actually exist on disk.
quote: Small models do this; checking the files instead of the words works in any language.

claim: Loop guard cuts a reply when a long passage repeats three times in a row.
quote: the same long passage back to back, three times over, means the model is stuck.

claim: Model picker targets roughly 15 tokens/second with room for context.
quote: picks the smartest one that stays above about 15 tokens a second with room for a decent context.

claim: Sandbox platform mechanisms: sandbox-exec (macOS), Landlock (Linux), low-integrity process (Windows).
quote: sandbox-exec on macOS, Landlock on Linux and a low-integrity process on Windows

claim: On Linux kernels without Landlock, sandboxed code runs unrestricted.
quote: Without Landlock (older kernels) the code runs unlimited.

claim: A tester found the local models too weak for real work.
quote: The models are really dumb, mainly.

claim: Commenters say many similar local AI apps already exist.
quote: So there are a zillion of these, including ones that do what yours does.

claim: Hob requires at least 8 GB RAM.
quote: Hob runs on Apple Silicon Macs, Windows PCs, and Linux, with at least 8 GB of memory (RAM).

claim: Windows build is not yet signed with a Microsoft certificate.
quote: Windows shows this for new apps that aren’t yet signed with a Microsoft certificate.

claim: No published benchmarks against other tools yet.
quote: Not yet, but that sounds like a useful overview to add to the landing page!

claim: Hob site states it is backed by Y Combinator.
